solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mathematician is one stroke short of a rogue

indicators.note: a capital R loses its slanting leg, one pen stroke, and becomes a P, so the first letter of the rogue's word is changed

parts.note: a rascal is a rogue or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A mathematician is described as only just falling short of being a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one stroke short of' turns the R of RASCAL into P: draw R, leave out its final diagonal stroke, and a P is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a seventeenth-century French mathematician and philosopher.

clue.text: Writer shows a measure of potential and a passion

parts.note: the volt is the unit of electrical potential difference
ire is anger, a violent passion

explanation.surface: An author displays both electric energy and strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Enlightenment author of Candide, a celebrated writer of satire and philosophy.

clue.text: Hallowed ground adult can't cross

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as its letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Sacred land that a grown-up is forbidden to walk across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun for land but is the past participle of grind, the anagram signal for A, CANT and CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hallowed is sacred and inviolable, too holy to be touched or tampered with.

clue.text: In hurry, Kelvin gets lift

indicators.note: the kelvin's letter goes in the word for hurry, placed within it

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning to hasten or hurry
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone called Kelvin, in a rush, is given a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelvin looks like a man's name but is the unit of temperature, symbol K.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike prices or a load is to raise it, an informal synonym of lift.

clue.text: Proust's a case of soporific waffle to make sense of

parts.note: Proust wrote in French, where the indefinite article 'a' is un

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: to waffle is to ramble on aimlessly

explanation.surface: A dig at Proust's long-winded prose as sleep-inducing waffle that needs deciphering.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust is not literary criticism here: the French writer simply signals that 'a' is to be put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a jumbled message is to make sense of it, restoring the intended order.

clue.text: Stop barring rear of public convenience!

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so a letter is kept out of the word for stop

parts.note: to cease is to stop

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A plea to stop closing off the back of a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public convenience' reads as one phrase meaning a toilet, but 'public' only gives its last letter C, and 'convenience' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease and convenience are synonyms for freedom from difficulty or effort, as in 'at your ease'.

clue.text: Second helpings of wholesome fare low in calories and salt

indicators.note: second helpings here means the second letter served up from each of the next words

parts.note: lite is the food-labelling spelling of light, low in calories

explanation.surface: A diet tip: go back for more healthy food that is low-calorie and salted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second helpings' sounds like greedy eating but picks the second letters, H and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is the mineral form of sodium chloride, rock salt.

clue.text: Move to new residence in high street with reduced rent

indicators.note: high as in drunk or intoxicated, so the letters of street stagger into a new order
reduced means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Relocating to a flat on the main shopping street because the rent was lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high street' looks like one phrase, but 'high' is the anagram signal for STREET (giving RESETT), and 'reduced' cuts LET to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to move people into a new home or region, establishing them afresh.

clue.text: Worship nowadays is accompanied by sermon

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of years
an oration is a formal speech, like a sermon

explanation.surface: Modern church services come with a homily.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep reverence or worship, especially of God.

clue.text: A break before Easter originally for religious feast

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the Easter letter

parts.note: a gap is a break or interval

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A holiday ahead of Easter, perhaps for a church celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An agape was the love feast shared by early Christians, a communal religious meal.

clue.text: Lake poet's cottage first of all for inner circle

parts.note: cot is a poetic or archaic word for a small cottage, and 'first of all' puts it ahead of the lake
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A Lake District poet's cottage, like Wordsworth's, as the hub of a literary clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake poet' suggests Wordsworth or Coleridge, but 'Lake' is ERIE and 'poet's cottage' is the poetic COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group sharing interests, an inner circle or clique.

clue.text: Something to wear in church, I seem to recollect

indicators.note: re-collect, gather again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely remembers a garment worn at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' reads as remember but is read as re-collect, the anagram signal for I SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a woman's loose shift or undergarment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Back in Abercrombie, laid a wreath

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read from right to left
in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In Abercrombie's past, a wreath was put down, perhaps at a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters IEL run across 'Abercrombie, laid'; 'Back' reads them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck, a kind of wreath.

clue.text: Program's usefulness ultimately has petered out

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so the last letter is taken
out as in wrong or inaccurate, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A piece of software's value has finally faded away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'petered out' looks like one phrase; 'out' alone is the anagram signal for S, HAS and PETERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreadsheet is a computer application for tabulating figures, a type of program.

clue.text: Made recording, originally stereo, in improved version — nothing less?

definitions.text: Made recording, originally stereo, in improved version — nothing less?

indicators.note: an improved version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged
originally points to the start of the word before it, its first letter
less means minus, so a letter is taken out of the word for the sound system

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A record has been re-released in better sound, first in stereo and fully reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: STEREO less O gives STERE; with MADE and R from recording, 'improved version' rearranges them, and the whole clue describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A remastered recording is a new improved edition produced from the original master tapes.

clue.text: Undressed wound requires injection of potassium salt first

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the inner letters go within the word for wound

parts.note: wound as in twisted and turned, like a snake: snaked

indicators.note: first says the sailor comes ahead of the potassium symbol

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, a tar
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: An unbandaged wound needs a shot of potassium salt first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind, i.e. SNAKED; 'salt' is a sailor, not a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked means completely nude, an emphatic form of undressed.

clue.text: Innocent European is framed by family

indicators.note: being framed means being surrounded, so the letter sits inside the family word

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

explanation.surface: A blameless European is set up by relatives, a miscarriage of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' plays on being set up for a crime, but here it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean record means a blameless one, so clean is a synonym of innocent.

clue.text: Jacket one wears in the morning only after college

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the college letter

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
one is the Roman numeral I
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A jacket someone wears in the morning, but only once out of college.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole was formerly a short jacket or sleeved bodice, before the word came to mean an undergarment.

clue.text: Cram round in mass close to celeb?

indicators.note: in places the circle letter inside the other two pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a round thing is circular, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Fans crowd in a mass close around a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: To mob a place is to crowd or pack into it, much as people cram into a space.

clue.text: Humble home with acre in front

indicators.note: in front says the acre letter comes before the word for home

parts.note: a base is a home or headquarters

explanation.surface: A modest house with an acre of land before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase is to humble or degrade, lowering someone in rank or esteem.

clue.text: Area I will need to take off? That's about right

definitions.text: Area I will need to take off? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the letter for right

parts.note: to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: A pilot asks whether a stretch of ground is what's needed for departure, and is told that's roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests flight, which fits the whole clue, but in the wordplay it means STRIP; 'That's' refers to A, I and STRIP, which go about R.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a cleared strip of land where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Meat that can be cooked quickly — is it nouvelle cuisine?

definitions.text: Meat that can be cooked quickly
definitions.meaning: a thin cut of beef fried for about a minute
nouvelle cuisine is mocked for its tiny portions, so its steak would be a minute, very small, one

explanation.definitionFit: A thin quick-fry beef cut, cooked in about sixty seconds; read as 'tiny steak' it suits fashionable small-portion cooking.

clue.text: Picked up near location of old Asian city

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the words are spoken and the sound gives the letters

parts.note: near is nigh and a location is a scene: nigh scene

explanation.surface: Something found close to an ancient city site in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH SCENE said aloud sounds like the adjective of Nicaea, the old city in Asia Minor (modern Iznik, Turkey).
explanation.definitionFit: Nicene describes Nicaea, the ancient Anatolian city that gave its name to the Nicene Creed.

clue.text: Eggs runny, over easy, for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first bits, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A breakfast order for eggs, runny and over easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over easy' is a US term for eggs fried on both sides, yolk still runny.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish's ovary.

clue.text: Man or woman regularly name dropping

indicators.note: dropping means falling lower, so in this down entry a letter moves further down

parts.note: evenly means regularly, at even intervals

explanation.surface: Someone, of either sex, habitually name-drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name dropping' looks like the social habit; here N literally drops from the middle of EVENLY to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a given name used for both males (Evelyn Waugh) and females.

clue.text: Fish do this to get mouse?

definitions.meaning: a mouse is slang for a black eye, which you get if someone hits your eye: sock (punch) plus eye

explanation.definitionFit: A red-fleshed Pacific salmon species; the second reading splits into punching an eye, which raises a bruise.

clue.text: For example, very large feelings of superiority

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A remark that, say, huge self-regard is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego, in plural, is a person's sense of self-importance, often an inflated sense of superiority.

clue.text: At heart sales patter's confusing hot air

indicators.note: confusing means muddling, so the letters are jumbled
the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: taken as its letters; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel is mostly baffling waffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'sales' is L; jumbled with PATTER it makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is idle, trivial chatter, the same as empty talk or hot air.

clue.text: Old statesman's depression apparent in speech

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: apparent in speech means the word is heard when spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A former politician's low mood is evident in how they talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood, but it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt, Elder and Younger, were eighteenth-century British prime ministers.

clue.text: Took at least some of Polonius's advice — slowly

definitions.text: Took at least some of Polonius's advice
definitions.meaning: Polonius in Hamlet warns 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'; someone who lent zero (nought, O) obeyed at least half of it
a musical tempo marking meaning slow

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian tempo direction for a slow pace in music; split as 'lent O' it means lending nothing.

clue.text: Wasted time in attempt to pursue old hand, perhaps

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow, so the following pieces come after the old letters

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: wasted as in ruined, so the letters of time are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frittered away time trying to catch a former labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hand' looks like a veteran, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay and 'hand, perhaps' is the definition by example; 'to pursue' means the attempt follows the old piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is an example of a limb's end, an extremity of the body, hence 'perhaps'.
